claim_boundary: This report records aggregate training metrics for private random/reward_selected/full_ledger splits. It does not include raw private trajectories or adapter weights. Downstream executable task completion is measured separately in benchmarks/executable-task-mlx-gemma4-e2b-adapters-512x4096-rawpython-mac5-2026-06-10.json.
training_objective_interpretation: On this larger 512-row/4096-token E2B run, validation loss ranks full_ledger first, random second, and reward_selected third. This differs from the earlier Gemma 3 1B/256-token run where reward_selected had the best validation loss. Downstream executable performance must therefore be reported separately instead of inferred from validation loss.
interpretation: The reward-selected adapter achieved the best downstream executable task result under the same Gemma 4 E2B 512-row/4096-token training setup, improving from random 3/6 to reward_selected 5/6 on the six-task hidden executable benchmark. Because the task set is small, this is a positive lift signal and proof that the evaluation path can detect nonzero trained-adapter differences, not a final broad SWE-style claim.
